name: Husqvarna Decompression Valve for 395XP
title: Husqvarna 395XP Decompression Valve: Replacement Part
h1: Husqvarna Decompression Valve for 395XP
meta: Replacement Husqvarna 395XP decompression valve. Restores easy pull-starts on the big 94 cc saw when the old valve leaks, sticks or loses compression.
tagline: The push-button valve that makes a 94 cc 395XP pull over without wrecking your shoulder.
summary: The Husqvarna 395XP decompression valve bleeds off compression while you pull the starter, so the big saw turns over without kicking the rope out of your hand. When the valve sticks open, leaks or gets damaged, the saw loses power or gets hard to start, and a new valve is the cheap fix.
highlights: Replacement decompression valve for the Husqvarna 395XP
Restores easy starting on a high-compression big-bore saw
Fixes compression loss from a leaking or stuck valve
Threads into the cylinder, no splitting the saw
Keeps your felling and bucking saw in service

p: The 395XP is a big-wood saw, and it makes serious compression. The decompression valve is what lets you start it on the ground or on a stump without a fight. Press the button, pull, and the valve pops closed on the first fire.

Signs of a bad valve: the button won't stay down, the saw loses power and feels down on compression, or you hear a hiss or see blow-by around the valve body. Carbon buildup can also hold it open after a long day of bucking.

A healthy valve matters more than it sounds. Without it, a 395XP is tiring to start all day, especially cold or when you are restarting it twenty times while bucking up a big removal. Starter ropes, pawls and handles also wear faster when they fight full compression. If you run a 395XP as the big-wood saw on the truck, it is worth keeping a spare valve in the parts box.

Remove the top cover, clean around the valve so grit doesn't fall into the cylinder, and unscrew the old valve with the right size socket. Thread the new one in by hand first, then snug it to the torque in the Husqvarna service manual. Don't overtighten into the aluminum cylinder.
Run the saw and check that the button resets on startup. Browse more Husqvarna chainsaw parts if you are refreshing the whole saw.

faq.q: How do I know my 395XP decompression valve is bad?
faq.a: Common signs are a button that won't stay pressed, hard starting, low compression or visible leaking around the valve body.

faq.q: Can I clean the old valve instead of replacing it?
faq.a: Sometimes carbon is the only problem and cleaning helps, but a valve that leaks or is damaged should be replaced.

name: Husqvarna Fuel Hose Assembly for T435 Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna T435 Fuel Hose Assembly: Replacement Fuel Line
h1: Husqvarna Fuel Hose Assembly for T435 Chainsaw
meta: Husqvarna T435 fuel hose assembly for the top-handle saw. Replace cracked or swollen fuel line to stop leaks, lean running and stalling up in the tree.
tagline: Fresh fuel line for the T435 top-handle when the old hose cracks, swells or leaks.
summary: The Husqvarna T435 fuel hose assembly replaces the line that carries fuel from the tank to the carburetor on the T435 top-handle saw. Old hose hardens and cracks with ethanol fuel and heat, and a pinhole leak is enough to make a climbing saw run lean, bog or quit mid-cut.
highlights: Replacement fuel hose assembly for the Husqvarna T435
Cures leaks, air leaks and lean running from old line
Fixes hard starting and stalling caused by cracked hose
Cheap preventive part for a hard-working climbing saw

p: A top-handle saw lives a rough life: heat from the engine, ethanol fuel, and days hanging off a saddle in the sun. Fuel hose goes stiff and cracks, especially where it passes through the tank. Once air gets drawn in, the T435 runs lean, idles poorly and can die when you tip it to cut.
If the saw smells of fuel, leaks from the tank area, or won't hold an idle after a carb clean, check the line first. It is one of the cheapest fixes on the saw.

The T435 is a light top-handle saw that many climbers use for pruning, small removals and detail work, so it often stays in service for years. That age shows up first in rubber parts. Replacing the fuel hose before it fails is cheaper than a service call, and it avoids the frustration of a saw that dies every time you hang it off the saddle and pull it back up to cut.

Drain the tank, pull the old hose and filter, and fit the new assembly so it seats fully in the tank grommet with the filter hanging free inside. Reattach to the carburetor and check for kinks. Reinstall the fuel filter or fit a new one at the same time.

Top-handle saws are for trained arborists working from a secure position. After any repair, confirm the chain brake and throttle lockout work before you climb. More T435 bits are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: How often should I replace the fuel hose on my T435?
faq.a: Inspect it every season and replace it as soon as it is hard, cracked or leaking. Many pros swap it with the fuel filter.

faq.q: Is this the same hose as other Husqvarna saws?
faq.a: Not always. Fuel line shape and length vary by model, so match the part to the T435.

name: Husqvarna Fuel Tank Oil Cap Assembly
title: Husqvarna Fuel Cap and Oil Tank Cap Assembly
h1: Husqvarna Fuel Tank Oil Cap Assembly
meta: Replacement Husqvarna fuel cap and oil tank cap assembly. Stops leaks and lost caps on the job. Check your saw model for the right fit before ordering.
tagline: Replacement tank cap for Husqvarna saws when the seal leaks or the cap goes missing.
summary: This Husqvarna fuel cap assembly replaces a leaking, cracked or lost cap on the fuel or bar oil tank of Husqvarna chainsaws. A cap that doesn't seal lets fuel and oil weep onto the saw, makes a mess of your saw box, and can pull the tank into a vacuum.
highlights: Complete cap assembly with seal
Stops weeping fuel or bar oil from a worn cap
Replaces caps lost on the job
Fits a range of Husqvarna chainsaws, check your model

p: Caps get dropped in the brush, cross-threaded on a cold morning, or the gasket goes flat after a few seasons. A leaking cap leaves fuel and bar oil all over the saw and anything it touches in the truck. Fuel near a hot muffler is a fire risk you don't need.
If your saw is leaking from the top of the tank, or the cap spins without tightening, a new cap assembly is the quick fix.

Fuel and bar oil caps also take abuse from gloves and cold. If a cap is hard to grip, has a broken bail or flip-up lever, or no longer clicks shut, replace it before it lets go on the job. A saw with a missing bar oil cap will run dry and cook its bar and chain quickly, and a missing fuel cap ends the day. Keeping one spare of each cap in the truck kit is cheap insurance.

Husqvarna uses several cap designs across its saw range, including flip-up caps and older screw caps. Match the cap style and your saw model before ordering. Fuel and oil caps are usually marked with a fuel pump or oil drop symbol.
Hand-tighten the cap until it seats, and check the seal is in place each time you fuel up. See the rest of our Husqvarna parts for filters, fuel lines and more.

faq.q: Will one cap fit every Husqvarna chainsaw?
faq.a: No. Husqvarna uses different cap styles across models, so confirm your saw model and cap type before ordering.

faq.q: Why does my saw leak oil when parked?
faq.a: A worn cap seal is a common cause, but a cracked tank or oil pump issue can also leak. Check the cap first.

name: Husqvarna Inlet Pipe Assembly for 550XP Mark II
title: Husqvarna 550XP Mark II Inlet Pipe Assembly: Intake Boot
h1: Husqvarna Inlet Pipe Assembly for 550XP Mark II
meta: Husqvarna 550XP Mark II inlet pipe assembly. Replace a split or hardened intake boot to stop air leaks, lean running and high revs on your 50 cc saw.
tagline: The intake boot between carb and cylinder on the 550XP Mark II. Air leak here kills saws.
summary: The Husqvarna 550XP Mark II inlet pipe assembly is the rubber intake boot that connects the carburetor to the cylinder. When it splits or hardens, the saw sucks unmetered air, runs lean and hot, and can score the piston, so it is one of the first parts to check on a saw that won't tune right.
highlights: Replacement inlet pipe (intake boot) for the 550XP Mark II
Cures air leaks that cause lean running and high idle
Protects the piston and cylinder from lean seizure
Fresh rubber seals properly at carb and cylinder

body.h: Symptoms of a bad inlet pipe
p: The 550XP Mark II is a popular ground and limbing saw, and it runs on AutoTune. A split intake boot lets in air the system can't account for. You may see a racing idle, surging, poor power, or a saw that bogs when you tip it. A pressure and vacuum test will confirm the leak.
Rubber gets brittle from heat and age, and a boot can also tear if the carb is pulled without care.

Because AutoTune keeps adjusting, an intake leak on a Mark II can hide for a while before it shows. The saw may run fine cold and then start acting up as it warms. If you have already cleaned the air filter, replaced the spark plug and checked the fuel filter and line, and the saw still surges or races, put the intake boot near the top of your list. It is a common failure on high-hour saws, and fixing it early protects the top end.

The job involves removing the air filter and carburetor to reach the boot. Seat the new inlet pipe fully on the cylinder intake and the carb side so it seals all the way around. A little care here beats chasing an air leak later.
After assembly, let the saw run and settle before working hard. Pair it with other Mark II parts from our chainsaw parts category.

faq.q: Is the 550XP Mark II inlet pipe the same as the original 550XP?
faq.a: No. The Mark II has its own intake parts, so order the part listed for your exact model.

faq.q: Can a bad intake boot damage my saw?
faq.a: Yes. An air leak makes the saw run lean and hot, which can score the piston and cylinder.

name: Husqvarna Inlet Pipe Assembly for 550XP Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 550XP Inlet Pipe Assembly: Replacement Boot
h1: Husqvarna Inlet Pipe Assembly for 550XP Chainsaw
meta: Replacement Husqvarna 550XP inlet pipe assembly for the original 550XP. Fix air leaks, lean running and a racing idle caused by a cracked intake boot.
tagline: Intake boot for the original 550XP. Stops air leaks that make the saw run lean.
summary: This Husqvarna 550XP inlet pipe assembly is the intake boot that joins the carburetor to the cylinder on the original 550XP. A cracked or loose boot lets in extra air, which shows up as surging, a high idle and lost power, and it can cook the top end if ignored.
highlights: Replacement inlet pipe for the original Husqvarna 550XP
Fixes air leaks between carb and cylinder
Helps AutoTune run the saw correctly
Inexpensive insurance for the piston and cylinder

p: On a fuel-injected or AutoTune saw, the electronics adjust fuel to the air they expect. An intake boot leak throws that off. The saw may sound like it is screaming at idle, hang at high revs, or fall off when you tip it into a cut. On a saw you use all day for limbing and bucking, you will feel it.
Old 550XPs are now old enough that the rubber is hardening, so the boot is worth checking on any saw that suddenly won't run right.

This page covers the part some old listings spelled as the intel pipe. It is the inlet pipe, the same part Husqvarna lists for the intake between carburetor and cylinder. If you are chasing a lean condition, check the impulse line and the crank seals as well, since they cause the same symptoms. A pressure and vacuum test will point you to the actual leak before you start replacing parts.

Remove the air filter and carburetor, then work the old boot off the cylinder. Clean the mating surfaces and press the new inlet pipe on until it seats evenly all the way around. Refit the carb and check that the throttle and choke move freely.
If you are not sure which 550XP you have, the Mark II has a different intake and its own part. More service parts are in our Husqvarna parts section.

faq.q: How do I tell an original 550XP from a Mark II?
faq.a: The Mark II is marked as such on the saw. Check the model label before ordering intake parts.

faq.q: What causes the inlet pipe to crack?
faq.a: Heat and age harden the rubber, and careless carb removal can tear it.

name: Husqvarna Knee Joint Assembly for 562XP
title: Husqvarna 562XP Knee Joint Assembly: Chain Brake Part
h1: Husqvarna Knee Joint Assembly for 562XP
meta: Husqvarna 562XP knee joint assembly for the chain brake linkage. Replace a worn or bent joint so the brake sets and releases cleanly on your 60 cc saw.
tagline: Chain brake linkage part for the 562XP. A brake that doesn't set right is not optional.
summary: The Husqvarna 562XP knee joint assembly is part of the chain brake linkage, the toggle that lets the brake band snap on when the handguard trips and hold off when you reset it. A worn or bent knee joint can make the brake sloppy, slow or hard to reset, and a chain brake has to work every time.
highlights: Replacement knee joint for the 562XP chain brake mechanism
Restores a crisp brake set and release
Fixes brakes that won't hold or won't reset
Original-fit part for the 562XP

body.h: When to look at the knee joint
p: Test the chain brake every day before work. Push the handguard forward with the saw off and it should snap on firmly. Pull it back and it should reset without binding. If the brake feels mushy, won't latch, or drags the chain with the guard back, the linkage needs attention.
Hard hits from a pinched bar, a dropped saw or a lot of sawdust packed into the clutch cover can bend or wear the knee joint.

On the 562XP, the brake mechanism sits under the clutch cover, where sawdust, bar oil and chips pack in quickly. A packed brake area can mimic a worn linkage, so clean it out before you condemn parts. If the brake still feels weak or inconsistent after a good cleaning, inspect the knee joint, the spring and the brake band together. Worn parts in the brake are not something to put off on a saw used for felling and bucking.

The brake spring is under strong tension, so use the procedure and tools in the Husqvarna service manual, or have a dealer do it. Clean the brake area, inspect the band for wear, and replace the knee joint as an assembly.
Never run a saw with a brake that doesn't work. Test it after the repair and again before the first cut. Find other 562XP parts in our chainsaw parts range.

faq.q: What does the knee joint do on a 562XP?
faq.a: It is the toggle in the chain brake mechanism that lets the brake band engage and release with the handguard.

faq.q: Can I keep using the saw if the brake is sloppy?
faq.a: No. Fix the chain brake before using the saw. It is a key kickback safety feature.

name: Husqvarna Micro Switch for T540iXP Battery Saw
title: Husqvarna T540iXP Micro Switch: Safety Switch Replacement
h1: Husqvarna Micro Switch for T540iXP Battery Saw
meta: Husqvarna T540iXP micro switch, the safety switch for the battery top-handle saw. Replace it when the saw won't run, cuts out or ignores trigger input.
tagline: The small safety switch that tells the T540iXP it is safe to run.
summary: The Husqvarna T540iXP micro switch is a safety switch in the battery top-handle saw that signals the controller when the handle controls are in position. When it fails, the saw may not start, may cut out under load, or may behave erratically, so it is a common fix on a saw that has battery and power but won't spin the chain.
highlights: Replacement micro (safety) switch for the T540iXP
Fixes no-run and intermittent cut-out faults
Part of the saw's safety interlock
Small part that can bring a battery climbing saw back to work

p: A battery saw lets you know when something is wrong with error lights on the keypad. If the battery is charged, the keypad powers up and the saw still won't run, or it cuts out as you squeeze the trigger, a worn or contaminated switch is a likely suspect. Sawdust and moisture work their way into handles over time.
Check the battery contacts and keypad first, then look at the switches in the handle.

Battery top-handle saws are popular with climbers because they are quiet, start instantly and need less engine maintenance. That doesn't mean they need none. Handles, switches and contacts still wear, especially on a saw that gets used daily in wet weather. Keep the handle area clean, store the saw dry, and don't hose it down. When a fault code shows up, check the manual for what it means before you start replacing parts.

Always remove the battery before opening the saw. Note how the switch is mounted and how the wiring is routed, then fit the new switch in the same position. Pinched wires cause more faults than they fix.

Top-handle saws are only for trained arborists working from a secure position in the tree. Confirm the saw only runs with the trigger and lockout engaged before going back aloft. See related T540iXP parts in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Why won't my T540iXP run with a charged battery?
faq.a: Possible causes include a fault in the battery contacts, keypad, trigger assembly or safety switch. The micro switch is a common culprit.

faq.q: Do I need to remove the battery to replace the switch?
faq.a: Yes. Always remove the battery before working inside a battery saw.

name: Husqvarna Recoil Starter Handle
title: Husqvarna Starter Handle: Recoil Pull Grip Replacement
h1: Husqvarna Recoil Starter Handle
meta: Replacement Husqvarna starter handle for recoil starters on chainsaws and other gear. Swap a cracked or lost pull grip when you replace starter rope.
tagline: A new pull grip for Husqvarna recoil starters. Cheap, and you'll want a spare.
summary: This Husqvarna starter handle is the pull grip on the end of the starter rope on Husqvarna recoil starters. Handles crack from being dropped and slammed back, and once one breaks the rope can whip back into the housing and leave you with a saw you can't start.
highlights: Replacement recoil starter handle
Fits a range of Husqvarna recoil starters, check your model
Good time to swap it is with new starter rope
Keep a spare in the saw kit

p: On the job, saws get started on the ground, on a stump, off a tailgate and in cold weather. Letting the rope snap back, or a hard drop on the handle side, eventually cracks the grip. A broken handle can also chew through the rope where it exits.
If the handle is cracked, sharp or spinning loose, swap it before it fails in the field.

A good handle also makes starting easier and safer. A cracked handle can pinch your glove or snap mid-pull, and a worn handle with a loose knot can let go and send the rope into the housing. On saws you start often, such as climbing saws and ground saws used for limbing and bucking, a new handle every season or two is reasonable. They are inexpensive, so keep one in the saw kit with a spare length of rope.

Pull the rope out, hold tension on the recoil so it doesn't retract, and feed the rope through the new handle. Tie a firm knot and seat it in the handle pocket. Check the rope too. If it is frayed, replace it at the same time.
Always let the rope rewind under control rather than letting go. More starter parts, including ropes, pulleys and springs, are in our Husqvarna parts section.

faq.q: Will this handle fit my Husqvarna saw?
faq.a: It fits many Husqvarna recoil starters, but handle styles vary, so check your model before ordering.

faq.q: Should I replace the starter rope too?
faq.a: If the rope is frayed or glazed, yes. Doing both at once saves a second job.

name: Husqvarna Replaceable Nose for PowerMatch Bars
title: Husqvarna Replaceable Bar Nose for PowerMatch Bars
h1: Husqvarna Replaceable Nose for PowerMatch Bars
meta: Husqvarna replaceable bar nose for PowerMatch guide bars. Swap a worn or seized sprocket nose and keep a good bar body in service for longer bucking work.
tagline: Replacement sprocket nose that puts a worn PowerMatch bar back to work.
summary: The Husqvarna replaceable bar nose fits Husqvarna PowerMatch guide bars, letting you replace a worn or seized sprocket nose without buying a whole new bar. On longer pro bars, the nose usually wears out before the rails, so this is the cheap way to get more life from a good bar.
highlights: Replacement sprocket nose for PowerMatch-style bars
Keeps a straight bar body in service
Fixes a seized, chipped or worn nose sprocket
Cheaper than a full bar on long pro lengths
specs: Husqvarna PowerMatch guide bars, match pitch and gauge

p: The nose sprocket takes the hardest wear on a bar, especially on a saw that does a lot of bore cuts, felling and dirty bucking. Signs it is done: the sprocket won't spin freely, teeth are worn or chipped, there is side play, or the nose gets hot fast. A seized nose will wreck chain quickly.
If the rails are still square and the bar is straight, a new nose is the right call.

PowerMatch is a Husqvarna name used on some pro bars and drive systems, and nose types differ by bar series, pitch and gauge. Before ordering, check the markings on your bar and match the nose to it. A wrong nose will not fit the rivet pattern or will not run the chain properly. If your bar does not have a replaceable nose, this part will not fit, and a new bar is the answer.

Replaceable noses are riveted on. Drill or grind out the old rivets, fit the new nose, and peen new rivets so the nose sits flush with the rails. Match the pitch and gauge of your bar and chain exactly. If you don't have the tools or the patience, a saw shop can do it quickly.
Dress the rails and check chain fit after the swap. More bar and saw parts are in our chainsaw parts category.

faq.q: Can I put this nose on any bar?
faq.a: No. It is made for bars designed for a replaceable nose. Match the bar type, pitch and gauge.

faq.q: How do I know the nose is worn out?
faq.a: A sprocket that binds, has worn or chipped teeth, or wobbles side to side should be replaced.

name: Husqvarna Replacement Nose for 3/8 Chainsaw Bars
title: Replacement Nose for 3/8 Chainsaw Bars by Husqvarna
h1: Husqvarna Replacement Nose for 3/8 Chainsaw Bars
meta: Husqvarna replacement nose for 3/8 chainsaw bars with a replaceable sprocket nose. Bring a worn bar back into service for felling and bucking work.
tagline: A 3/8-pitch sprocket nose for Husqvarna bars built to take a replaceable nose.
summary: This Husqvarna replacement nose for 3/8 chainsaw bars swaps out a worn sprocket nose on bars made with a replaceable nose. When the rails are still good but the nose is tired, binding or chipped, fitting a new nose keeps a straight bar working for a fraction of the price of a new one.
highlights: Replacement sprocket nose for 3/8 inch pitch bars
For bars designed with a replaceable nose
Restores free-spinning nose sprocket
Extends the life of long bars on bigger saws

p: 3/8 pitch bars run on mid and large saws used for felling, bucking and storm cleanup. On those saws the nose sprocket wears first, especially if you bore cut a lot or run a dull chain. A bar with good rails and a dead nose is still worth saving.
Look for a sprocket that won't spin freely, has chipped teeth or rocks side to side. Any of those means it's time.

Long 3/8 pitch bars are expensive, so getting more life out of them makes sense for crews running big saws. Keep the nose greased, flip the bar regularly so the rails wear evenly, and keep the chain sharp so you are not forcing the bar through the cut. When the nose is finally worn out, replacing it is the cheapest way to keep a good bar in the rotation for another season.

Grind or drill out the old rivets, fit the new nose with matching gauge, and set new rivets so they sit flush. The nose must be centered with the rails or the chain will ride rough. If you'd rather not peen rivets, a saw shop does this job routinely.
Grease the nose sprocket through the bar's grease hole regularly once it's in service. See more bar parts in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Does this fit .404 pitch bars?
faq.a: No. This nose is for 3/8 inch pitch bars. Match pitch and gauge to your bar and chain.

faq.q: Do I need special tools?
faq.a: You need a way to remove the old rivets and peen new ones. Many people have a saw shop do it.

name: Husqvarna Screw for T540iXP Clutch Side
title: Husqvarna T540iXP Screw for the Clutch Side
h1: Husqvarna Screw for T540iXP Clutch Side
meta: Replacement Husqvarna T540iXP screw for the clutch side of the battery top-handle saw. Replace a stripped or lost screw so covers and parts stay tight.
tagline: A replacement screw for the drive side of the T540iXP battery top-handle.
summary: This Husqvarna T540iXP screw fits the clutch side (drive side) of the battery top-handle saw, the side where the sprocket, bar and chain run. Lost or stripped screws on a climbing saw are a small problem that can turn into a loose cover or rattling part, so replace them with the right one rather than whatever is in the truck.
highlights: Correct replacement screw for the T540iXP clutch side
Replaces stripped, lost or damaged screws
Right length and thread for the saw
Small part, keeps a climbing saw tight

p: Husqvarna parts diagrams still call the chain side of the T540iXP the clutch side, even though it is a battery saw. Screws on that side hold parts that take vibration and chain loads all day. A screw that is too long can bottom out or hit internal parts, and one too short can strip the housing.
Check the parts diagram for your saw to confirm the screw position before ordering.

On a battery top-handle saw used daily, it pays to check screws on a regular schedule. Vibration, heat from cutting and being hung off a saddle loosen fasteners over time. A missing screw on the bar side can lead to a loose cover or brake part, which affects how the saw handles in the tree. Keep a couple of spare screws in the climbing kit so you can fix it on the spot.

Remove the battery first. Clean the threads, start the screw by hand, and tighten it snug without overdoing it, since many threads on a top-handle saw are in plastic or light alloy. A dab of thread locker is sometimes specified, so follow the service manual.
Top-handle saws are for trained arborists. Check the chain brake and that everything is tight before you climb. More T540iXP parts are in our chainsaw parts category.

faq.q: Why is it called the clutch side on a battery saw?
faq.a: Husqvarna's parts lists use the same side names across saws. On the T540iXP it means the bar and chain side.

faq.q: Can I use a hardware-store screw instead?
faq.a: It is better to use the correct part. Length, thread and head type matter in a small housing.

name: Husqvarna Screw for 395XP Muffler Support
title: Husqvarna 395XP Muffler Screw for Muffler Support
h1: Husqvarna Screw for 395XP Muffler Support
meta: Husqvarna 395XP muffler screw for the muffler support. Replace a lost or stripped screw so the muffler stays tight on the big saw and doesn't crack.
tagline: The screw that holds the 395XP muffler support. Lose it and things shake loose.
summary: This Husqvarna 395XP muffler screw secures the muffler support on the 395XP. A big-bore saw shakes hard, and if a muffler screw backs out the muffler can rattle, crack, leak exhaust or let hot gases near parts that shouldn't see them.
highlights: Replacement screw for the 395XP muffler support
Keeps the muffler tight on a high-vibration saw
Replaces lost, stripped or rusted screws
Correct thread and length for the location

p: On a 94 cc saw used for felling and bucking big wood, muffler hardware takes a beating from heat and vibration. Make checking it part of routine service. A loose muffler often shows up as a new rattle, black soot around the joint, or a muffler that moves when you push on it.
Running with loose muffler hardware can crack the muffler or damage the gasket and the cylinder threads.

The 395XP is often the biggest saw on a tree truck, used for felling big trees, bucking trunk wood and storm cleanup. It also produces a lot of heat and vibration, so muffler hardware gets loose more often than on smaller saws. Keeping a few spare screws for the muffler and support in the parts bin saves a lot of downtime. Check them every time you clean the saw.

Let the saw cool fully. Clean the threads and fit the new screw, then tighten to the torque in the service manual. Heat cycles can loosen exhaust fasteners, so check them again after the first few hours of running.
If the gasket is burnt or broken, replace it at the same time. More 395XP parts are in our Husqvarna chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Why do muffler screws come loose?
faq.a: Heat cycles and heavy vibration on big saws loosen exhaust fasteners over time.

faq.q: Should I replace the muffler gasket too?
faq.a: If it is burnt, torn or leaking, yes. Fit it while the muffler is off.

name: Husqvarna Screw for Anti-Vibration Mount
title: Husqvarna Anti Vibration Mount Screw Replacement
h1: Husqvarna Screw for Anti-Vibration Mount
meta: Replacement Husqvarna anti vibration mount screw for chainsaw AV springs and buffers. Keep handles tight and vibration damping working as designed.
tagline: The screw that holds a Husqvarna AV spring or buffer in place.
summary: This Husqvarna anti vibration mount screw secures the springs or rubber buffers that isolate the handles from the engine on Husqvarna chainsaws. When an AV screw goes missing, the handle gets sloppy, vibration climbs, and the remaining mounts take extra strain.
highlights: Replacement screw for Husqvarna anti-vibration mounts
Keeps AV springs and buffers secured
Restores a solid handle feel
Check your saw model for the right screw

p: Anti-vibration mounts are the reason you can run a saw all day without your hands going numb. Over months of bucking and limbing, mounts and their screws work loose or break. A saw with a loose AV mount feels wobbly in the rear or top handle and transmits more vibration to your hands and arms.
Long-term vibration exposure is a real health risk for saw operators, so keep the AV system in good shape.

AV springs and buffers are part of what separates a pro saw from a cheap one. On Husqvarna pro saws, the AV system is designed so the handles float on springs or buffers, and each mount depends on its screws to stay in place. If a screw goes missing, the remaining mounts take extra load and wear faster. Fix it as soon as you notice it, not at the end of the season.

Confirm the screw for your saw model, as length and thread vary by mount. Clean the threads, seat the spring or buffer correctly, and tighten to spec. Use thread locker only where the service manual calls for it.
If a spring is broken or a rubber buffer is torn, replace it too. Find mounts and other parts in our chainsaw parts category.

faq.q: How do I know if an AV mount is loose?
faq.a: A handle that moves more than it should, new rattles, or a big jump in vibration are common signs.

faq.q: Does one screw fit all Husqvarna AV mounts?
faq.a: No. Screw size varies by saw and mount position. Check your model's parts list.

name: Husqvarna Screw for Chain Brake Handle
title: Husqvarna Chain Brake Handle Screw: Replacement
h1: Husqvarna Screw for Chain Brake Handle
meta: Replacement Husqvarna chain brake handle screw for the handguard. Replace a lost or stripped screw so the brake handle stays secure and works properly.
tagline: The screw that holds the handguard to the brake mechanism on Husqvarna saws.
summary: This Husqvarna chain brake handle screw secures the front handguard (chain brake handle) on Husqvarna chainsaws. If it loosens or goes missing, the handguard can wobble or fail to trip the brake properly, and that is a safety problem you need to fix before the next cut.
highlights: Replacement screw for the chain brake handle
Keeps the handguard tight to the brake mechanism
Replaces lost, stripped or damaged screws
Check your saw model for fit

body.h: A loose handguard is a safety issue
p: The handguard is the trip for the chain brake, which protects you in a kickback. If the screw holding it loosens, the guard can move off position and the brake may not engage reliably. A wobbly handguard is often the first sign.
Test the brake every day: with the saw stopped, push the guard forward and it should snap on firmly, then reset cleanly.

Chain brakes are especially important for climbers and anyone doing felling and bucking where kickback is a risk. A saw with a loose handguard is not ready to work. If the guard is cracked or the brake is weak after you fit a new screw, look at the brake mechanism itself, including the spring, band and linkage. A dealer can help if you are not comfortable working on the brake. Keep a spare screw in the saw kit.

Confirm the screw for your saw model. Clean the threads, fit the handguard in its correct position, and tighten to the service manual's spec. Check for a cracked guard while you are there, since a broken guard should be replaced too.
Test the brake before running the saw. More brake and saw parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: What happens if the chain brake handle is loose?
faq.a: The brake may not engage reliably in a kickback. Fix it before using the saw.

faq.q: Is this screw the same across all Husqvarna saws?
faq.a: No. Check your model's parts list to confirm the right screw.

name: Husqvarna Screw
title: Husqvarna Chainsaw Screw: Genuine Replacement Fastener
h1: Husqvarna Screw
meta: Replacement Husqvarna chainsaw screw for covers, housings and components. Match the part to your model's diagram before ordering to get the right fit.
tagline: A replacement Husqvarna fastener. Confirm the location and size on your parts diagram.
summary: This Husqvarna chainsaw screw is a replacement fastener for Husqvarna power equipment. Saws shake loose screws, strip them in plastic housings and drop them in the leaves, and the right replacement keeps covers and components tight without forcing the wrong thread into a housing.
highlights: Replacement Husqvarna fastener
Confirm the location against your model's parts diagram
Avoids stripping housings with the wrong screw
Handy to keep spares of common sizes in the saw box

p: Husqvarna uses many different screws across its saws, with different lengths, threads and heads for covers, handles, mufflers and mounts. Before ordering, find your saw's model and serial number and look up the parts diagram for the location you need. Matching the part number is the only reliable way to get the right one.
Using a screw that is too long can bottom out against internal parts. Too short, and it may strip the threads.

Many old listings for small parts like this simply say screw. That makes it hard to know where it fits without the part number. If you are not sure which screw you need, compare the old screw against the parts diagram, or bring the saw to a dealer. Common locations include covers, handles, the muffler, the chain brake and AV mounts. Fasteners are cheap, so keep a few spares of the screws you lose most often.
Clean the threads, start the screw by hand, and tighten it to spec. Threads in plastic and magnesium housings strip easily, so don't overdo it. Use thread locker only where Husqvarna specifies it.
Do a quick walk-around of your saw's fasteners during regular service so loose screws get caught early. Browse more Husqvarna parts for your saw.

faq.q: How do I know this is the screw I need?
faq.a: Check your saw's parts diagram and match the part number for the location you are repairing.

faq.q: Why do chainsaw screws come loose?
faq.a: Vibration and heat loosen fasteners over time. Check them during routine service.

name: Husqvarna Seal for 372XP X-Torque Clutch Side
title: Husqvarna 372XP X-Torque Crankshaft Seal: Clutch Side
h1: Husqvarna Seal for 372XP X-Torque Clutch Side
meta: Husqvarna 372XP X-Torque crankshaft seal for the clutch side. Replace a leaking seal to stop air leaks, a high idle and lean running on your 70 cc saw.
tagline: Clutch-side crank seal for the 372XP X-Torque. Keeps the crankcase airtight.
summary: This Husqvarna 372XP X-Torque crankshaft seal fits the clutch side of the crankcase. A two-stroke needs an airtight crankcase to run right, and a worn crank seal draws in extra air, causing a high or hanging idle, lean running and the risk of a scored piston.
highlights: Clutch-side crankshaft seal for the 372XP X-Torque
Cures crankcase air leaks
Fixes a high idle and lean running from a bad seal
Protects the engine from lean damage

body.h: Signs of a leaking crank seal
p: The 372XP X-Torque is a strong mid-size saw for felling and bucking. If it starts racing at idle, won't hold a tune, or runs hot and lean even after a carb clean, a crank seal may be leaking. On the clutch side, seals can also be damaged by heat from a slipping clutch.
A pressure and vacuum test is the best way to confirm the leak before you tear into the saw.

Crank seals harden with age and heat, and saws that sit for long periods are especially prone to seal problems. A seal leak can also come from a crankshaft with too much end play or from damage during a previous repair. If you are replacing one seal, check the other one too, since both are the same age. A fresh pair of seals can make an older 372XP X-Torque run like it should again.

Remove the clutch, oil pump drive and other parts to reach the seal. Pry out the old seal without scratching the crankshaft or the case, then press the new one in square to the correct depth. A light coat of oil on the lip helps it seat without damage.
If you are not set up for this job, a saw shop can do it quickly. Find more 372XP parts in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: How do I know if my crank seal is leaking?
faq.a: Common signs are a high or hanging idle and lean running. A pressure and vacuum test confirms it.

faq.q: Should I replace both crank seals at once?
faq.a: Many mechanics do, since both have the same age and wear. Check the flywheel side seal while the saw is apart.

name: Husqvarna Spring Cassette Assembly for 592XP Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 592XP Recoil Spring Cassette Assembly
h1: Husqvarna Spring Cassette Assembly for 592XP Chainsaw
meta: Husqvarna 592XP recoil spring cassette assembly for the starter. Replace a broken spring so the rope rewinds properly on the big 90 cc class saw.
tagline: Starter recoil spring cassette for the 592XP. Rope won't rewind, this is likely why.
summary: The Husqvarna 592XP recoil spring cassette assembly is the spring pack inside the starter that rewinds the rope after each pull. When the spring breaks or loses tension, the rope hangs out of the housing or rewinds weakly, and a big-bore saw becomes hard to start.
highlights: Recoil spring cassette for the 592XP starter
Spring comes in a cassette for safer handling
Fixes a starter rope that won't rewind
Restores normal starting on a big-bore saw

p: The 592XP is a big felling and bucking saw, and its starter works hard. Letting the rope snap back, pulling it out to the end of its travel, and sawdust inside the starter all wear the recoil spring. A broken spring means the rope stays out, which is a quick way to tear up the starter or the rope.
If the rope doesn't return or returns slowly, check the spring before you replace the whole starter.

Big saws are harder to start than small ones, and the starter on a 592XP gets pulled hard. Keep the starter area clean and free of sawdust, pull the rope straight out, and don't let the handle snap back. Those habits help the spring and rope last longer. If you replace the cassette and the rope still doesn't rewind properly, check the starter pulley and the rope routing.

Remove the starter housing and release any rope tension. Pull out the old cassette, clean the housing, and fit the new one. The cassette design keeps the spring contained, which is safer than handling a loose recoil spring. Wear eye protection anyway.
Re-wind and pre-tension the rope according to the service manual. Find more 592XP starter parts in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Why won't my 592XP starter rope rewind?
faq.a: A broken or weak recoil spring is the most common cause. Debris in the starter or a damaged pulley can also cause it.

faq.q: Do I need the whole starter or just the spring cassette?
faq.a: If the housing, pulley and pawls are fine, the cassette alone is usually enough.

name: Husqvarna Starter Assembly for 460 Rancher
title: Husqvarna 460 Rancher Starter Assembly: Recoil Replacement
h1: Husqvarna Starter Assembly for 460 Rancher
meta: Complete Husqvarna 460 Rancher starter assembly. Replace a cracked housing, broken recoil or worn pulley and get the saw starting cleanly again.
tagline: Complete recoil starter for the 460 Rancher. Bolt it on and pull.
summary: The Husqvarna 460 Rancher starter assembly is a complete recoil starter for the 460 Rancher. When the housing is cracked, the rope won't rewind, or the starter slips, a full assembly is often quicker and more reliable than rebuilding piece by piece.
highlights: Complete recoil starter assembly for the 460 Rancher
Fixes slipping, binding or non-rewinding starters
Replaces cracked or broken housings
Quick bolt-on fix

body.h: When to replace the whole starter
p: The 460 Rancher is a popular saw for firewood, storm cleanup and ground work on tree crews. Its starter takes a lot of pulls, and the housing can crack if the saw is dropped or tossed into the truck. If the rope won't return, the starter slips without turning the engine, or the housing is broken, a complete assembly gets you back running fast.
Rebuilding with individual parts works too, but if several pieces are worn, the full assembly is often the better buy.

The 460 Rancher is popular with homeowners and crews alike for firewood, storm cleanup and ground work. Because it gets used by a lot of different people, starters often take abuse: rope yanked at an angle, the saw started on the ground without a firm grip, or dropped on the starter side. A new starter assembly is an easy fix, and it often brings a saw that has been hard to start back to life.

Remove the screws holding the old starter to the saw, lift it off, and clean the flywheel area of sawdust. Fit the new assembly, making sure the pawls engage the flywheel correctly, then tighten the screws evenly.
Pull the rope slowly a few times to make sure it engages and rewinds smoothly before starting the saw. More 460 Rancher parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Is the 460 Rancher starter easy to replace?
faq.a: Yes. It is held on by a few screws and swaps in a few minutes.

faq.q: Why does my starter slip without turning the engine?
faq.a: Worn or broken pawls or a damaged flywheel engagement are common causes.

name: Husqvarna Starter Assembly for T540XP Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna T540XP Starter Assembly: Top-Handle Recoil
h1: Husqvarna Starter Assembly for T540XP Chainsaw
meta: Husqvarna T540XP starter assembly for the gas top-handle saw. Replace a cracked housing or failed recoil so your climbing saw starts reliably in the tree.
tagline: A complete recoil starter for the T540XP gas top-handle saw.
summary: The Husqvarna T540XP starter assembly is a complete recoil starter for the T540XP gas top-handle chainsaw. A climbing saw has to start when you need it, and a cracked housing, slipping pawl or broken recoil spring on a top-handle saw costs time and energy in the tree.
highlights: Complete starter assembly for the T540XP
Fixes non-rewinding, slipping or cracked starters
Quick bolt-on replacement
Keeps your climbing saw starting reliably

p: Top-handle saws are started over and over during a climb, and they hang on a lanyard and bounce off the trunk. The starter housing takes hits, and the rope and recoil spring see more cycles than on many ground saws. If the rope won't return, the starter slips, or the housing is cracked, replace the assembly.
Check that you have the T540XP and not the battery T540iXP, which has no recoil starter.

A reliable starter matters more on a climbing saw than on most others. You often start a top-handle saw while tied in, so a starter that slips or a rope that won't rewind means extra effort and time in the tree. Keeping the starter clean and replacing worn parts promptly helps you work smoothly. If the housing is cracked, replace the full assembly rather than patching it.

Remove the screws holding the starter, lift it off, and clean the flywheel area. Fit the new starter, ensuring the pawls engage, and tighten the screws evenly. Test the pull gently a few times before starting the saw.

Top-handle saws are for trained arborists working from a secure position. Start the saw safely according to the manual and check the chain brake before climbing. More T540XP parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Does this fit the T540iXP battery saw?
faq.a: No. The T540iXP is battery powered and has no recoil starter. This is for the gas T540XP.

faq.q: Can I replace just the rope or spring?
faq.a: Yes, if the rest of the starter is in good shape. A full assembly makes sense when several parts are worn or the housing is damaged.

name: Husqvarna Starter Pawl and Spring Kit for 572XP Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 572XP Starter Pawl and Spring Kit
h1: Husqvarna Starter Pawl and Spring Kit for 572XP Chainsaw
meta: Husqvarna 572XP starter pawl and spring kit. Replace worn pawls and weak springs when the starter slips or won't engage the flywheel on your 70 cc saw.
tagline: Pawls and springs for the 572XP starter, for a rope that pulls but won't turn the engine.
summary: The Husqvarna 572XP starter pawl and spring kit replaces the pawls and springs that engage the flywheel when you pull the starter rope. When pawls wear or springs weaken, the rope pulls freely without turning the engine, or catches only some of the time.
highlights: Starter pawls and springs for the 572XP
Fixes slipping or intermittent starter engagement
Cheaper than a complete starter
Restores a positive catch on the flywheel

p: The 572XP is a high-power saw for felling and bucking. If you pull the rope and it spins freely, or catches only now and then, check the pawls on the flywheel side. Worn pawl tips, weak springs, or packed-in sawdust stop the pawls from swinging out and catching the starter pulley.
Clean the area first. If the pawls are rounded or the springs are stretched, replace them as a set.

Pawls are small parts, but they take a lot of force on a 70 cc class saw. Each time you pull the starter, the pawls catch the pulley and turn the engine against compression. Over time the tips round off and the springs weaken. If you are rebuilding the starter, check the pulley, rope and recoil spring at the same time. A complete refresh is often worth it on a high-hour saw.

Remove the starter housing to expose the flywheel. Take off the old pawls and springs, noting how they are mounted, then fit the new parts in the same orientation. Make sure the pawls move freely and spring back.
Refit the starter and test with slow pulls before starting the saw. More 572XP parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Why does my 572XP starter rope pull without turning the engine?
faq.a: Worn pawls or weak pawl springs are the most common cause.

faq.q: Should I replace both pawls?
faq.a: Yes. Replace them as a set so they wear evenly.

name: Husqvarna Starter Pulley for 592XP
title: Husqvarna 592XP Starter Pulley: Recoil Rope Pulley
h1: Husqvarna Starter Pulley for 592XP
meta: Husqvarna 592XP starter pulley for the recoil starter. Replace a cracked or worn pulley that slips, binds or chews rope on your big-bore saw.
tagline: The rope pulley inside the 592XP starter. Cracked pulley, chewed rope, no start.
summary: The Husqvarna 592XP starter pulley is the rope drum inside the recoil starter that the rope winds on and the pawls catch. A cracked or worn pulley can slip, bind or fray the rope, and on a big saw that takes a lot of pulling, that is a problem you notice fast.
highlights: Replacement starter pulley for the 592XP
Fixes slipping, binding or rope-chewing starters
Pairs well with new rope and spring cassette
Original-fit part for the 592XP

p: On a big-bore saw like the 592XP, the starter pulley gets yanked hard. Over time the hub wears, the edges crack, or the notches the pawls catch get rounded. Symptoms include a starter that slips, a rope that frays quickly, or a pulley that wobbles on its shaft.
If the rope keeps breaking, look at the pulley before replacing the rope again.

The 592XP is a big-bore saw for felling large trees and bucking big wood, and the starter pulley is one of the parts that takes the most strain. If you are replacing the pulley, check the rope, the spring cassette and the pawls at the same time. A complete starter refresh can save you from multiple breakdowns on the job. Keep the starter area clean and free of sawdust to extend the life of all the parts.

Remove the starter housing, release the spring tension, and take off the old pulley. Check the spring cassette, then fit the new pulley and wind on fresh rope if needed. Set the rope pre-tension per the service manual.
Pull the rope slowly a few times after assembly to confirm the pawls catch and the rope rewinds fully.
Wear eye protection when working near recoil springs. More 592XP starter parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Why does my starter rope keep breaking?
faq.a: A cracked or worn pulley, a sharp-edged guide or a weak recoil spring can all fray rope quickly.

faq.q: Should I replace the rope at the same time?
faq.a: If it is frayed, yes. Fit new rope when the starter is apart.

name: Husqvarna Starter Rope for 550XP Mark II
title: Husqvarna 550XP Starter Rope for the Mark II
h1: Husqvarna Starter Rope for 550XP Mark II
meta: Husqvarna 550XP starter rope for the Mark II. Replace a frayed or broken pull cord before it snaps on the job and keep your 50 cc saw starting reliably.
tagline: Fresh starter rope for the 550XP Mark II. Swap it before it snaps.
summary: This Husqvarna 550XP starter rope is cut for the 550XP Mark II recoil starter. Starter rope frays from wear at the housing guide and from being yanked at angles, and a snapped rope at the start of a job means a saw that won't run.
highlights: Replacement starter rope for the 550XP Mark II
Correct diameter and length for the starter
Replace at the first sign of fraying
Cheap part to keep in the saw kit

p: The 550XP Mark II is a workhorse for limbing, bucking and ground cleanup, and it gets started a lot every day. Check the rope at the handle and where it exits the housing. If it is frayed, glazed or thin, replace it. It is a lot easier to swap at the shop than to deal with a snapped rope on site.
If the rope wears fast, check the rope guide in the housing for sharp edges.

Rope wear is often a symptom of other problems. Check the starter pulley, the rope guide and the spring cassette for wear while the starter is apart. A cracked rope guide or worn pulley can fray new rope quickly. Pull the rope straight out from the saw, not at an angle, and don't let the handle snap back. Those habits make the rope and starter last much longer.

Remove the starter, release the spring tension, and pull out the old rope. Feed the new rope through the pulley and housing, tie the knots securely, and wind it on with the pre-tension the service manual calls for. The rope should pull out fully with a little spring left over.
Pair it with a new handle if the old one is cracked. More 550XP parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: How often should I replace the starter rope?
faq.a: Replace it as soon as it is frayed or glazed. Many pros swap it once a season on a daily-use saw.

faq.q: Why does my rope keep fraying?
faq.a: Pulling at an angle, a sharp rope guide or a damaged pulley can wear rope fast.

name: Husqvarna T540iXP Chassis for Flywheel Side
title: Husqvarna T540iXP Chassis, Flywheel Side: Replacement
h1: Husqvarna T540iXP Chassis for Flywheel Side
meta: Husqvarna T540iXP chassis for the flywheel side of the battery top-handle saw. Replace a cracked or damaged housing half and get the saw back in the tree.
tagline: Replacement flywheel-side housing half for the T540iXP battery top-handle saw.
summary: This Husqvarna T540iXP chassis is the flywheel-side housing half of the battery top-handle saw. Top-handle saws get dropped, banged against trunks and hung off saddles, and a cracked chassis can let in dust and moisture or leave internal parts loose.
highlights: Flywheel-side chassis for the T540iXP
Replaces cracked or broken housing halves
Keeps dust and moisture out of the motor and electronics
Original-fit part

p: Husqvarna's parts diagrams use the terms flywheel side and clutch side for the two chassis halves, even on the battery saw. If the flywheel-side half is cracked, has broken screw bosses, or won't hold the other parts tight, replacing it is the right fix.
A damaged housing can let sawdust and water reach the motor and electronics, which leads to bigger repairs.

Battery top-handle saws are lighter and quieter than gas saws, but the housing still has to hold the motor, electronics and bar together under load. A cracked chassis can let in moisture and dust, cause wires to chafe and lead to intermittent faults. If you see cracks after a fall or rough handling, replace the chassis half before it causes more problems. Inspect the saw after any drop.

Remove the battery first. Taking a battery saw apart to swap a chassis half is a careful job: note wire routing and component positions, and transfer the parts to the new housing. Many owners have a dealer do it.

Top-handle saws are for trained arborists working from a secure position. Test all controls and the chain brake after reassembly. Find the matching clutch-side chassis and more parts in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: What is the flywheel side on a battery saw?
faq.a: It is Husqvarna's parts-list name for the side opposite the bar and chain.

faq.q: Is this a DIY job?
faq.a: It can be, but it involves moving the motor and electronics. A dealer can do it if you are unsure.

name: Husqvarna T540iXP Clutch Side Chassis
title: Husqvarna T540iXP Clutch Side Chassis: Replacement
h1: Husqvarna T540iXP Clutch Side Chassis
meta: Husqvarna T540iXP clutch side chassis, the housing half on the bar side of the battery top-handle saw. Replace it when cracked or with stripped bosses.
tagline: Replacement bar-side housing half for the T540iXP battery top-handle saw.
summary: This Husqvarna T540iXP clutch side chassis is the housing half on the bar and chain side of the battery top-handle saw. It carries the bar mount area and takes chain loads, so a cracked chassis or stripped bosses on this side affect how solidly the bar is held.
highlights: Clutch-side (bar side) chassis for the T540iXP
Replaces cracked or broken housing halves
Restores a solid bar mount area
Original-fit part

body.h: Signs you need a new chassis
p: Look for cracks around the bar studs, the chain brake area or the screw bosses. If the bar won't stay tight, screws won't hold, or you see a crack after a fall, the clutch-side chassis may need replacing.
Battery saws don't have a clutch, but Husqvarna's parts lists still use the clutch side name for the bar and chain side.

This side of the chassis holds the bar mount, so damage here affects how well the bar stays tight and how the chain tracks. If you have trouble keeping chain tension, or the bar shifts under load even with the bar nut tight, inspect this side of the chassis for cracks or worn bosses. On a climbing saw, a loose bar is not something to ignore. Replace the chassis half if it is damaged.
Remove the battery before starting. Transfer the motor, chain brake and other parts carefully, noting how everything goes together. A dealer can do this if you are unsure.
If both halves are damaged, replace them together so screw bosses and seams line up properly.
Test all controls, the chain brake and chain tension after reassembly. Top-handle saws are for trained arborists only. Find the flywheel-side chassis and other parts in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Why is it called the clutch side if the saw is battery powered?
faq.a: Husqvarna uses the same side names across its parts lists. It means the bar and chain side.

faq.q: Can I keep using a saw with a cracked chassis?
faq.a: It is not recommended, especially near the bar mount or brake. Replace it before use.

name: Husqvarna T540iXP Trigger Assembly
title: Husqvarna T540iXP Trigger Assembly: Replacement Part
h1: Husqvarna T540iXP Trigger Assembly
meta: Husqvarna T540iXP trigger assembly for the battery top-handle saw. Replace a worn, sticking or broken trigger so the saw responds properly in the tree.
tagline: Replacement trigger for the T540iXP. Smooth throttle and a lockout that works.
summary: The Husqvarna T540iXP trigger assembly controls chain speed on the battery top-handle saw. A sticking, broken or unresponsive trigger makes a climbing saw unsafe and frustrating, so replace it rather than work around it.
highlights: Replacement trigger assembly for the T540iXP
Fixes sticking, broken or unresponsive triggers
Restores smooth speed control
Works with the trigger lockout

p: The trigger on a top-handle saw sees constant use, and sawdust, sap and drops wear it down. If the trigger sticks, doesn't return, feels gritty, or the saw doesn't respond properly, check the trigger assembly. A trigger that doesn't spring back is a safety problem.
Also check the trigger lockout, which should stop the trigger from moving unless it is pressed.

On a battery saw, the trigger controls an electronic speed controller, so it needs to move smoothly and return reliably. Climbers who use the T540iXP for pruning and removals pull the trigger thousands of times a day, so wear is expected over time. Keep the handle area clean, store the saw dry and avoid washing it with water. A smooth, reliable trigger makes the saw safer and more comfortable to use.
Remove the battery. Open the handle, note how the trigger, springs and lockout fit together, and install the new assembly in the same way. Make sure wires and switches are not pinched.
Never tie, tape or wedge a trigger or lockout to get around a fault. Fix the part instead.

After assembly, check that the trigger only works with the lockout pressed and returns fully when released. Top-handle saws are for trained arborists. More T540iXP parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Why is my T540iXP trigger sticking?
faq.a: Sawdust, sap or a worn or broken spring are common causes. Clean it first and replace if needed.

faq.q: Does the trigger assembly include the lockout?
faq.a: Check the parts diagram for your saw. Contents can vary.

name: Husqvarna Worm Wheel for 550XP Mark II
keyword: husqvarna 550xp mark ii oil pump worm gear
title: Husqvarna 550XP Mark II Oil Pump Worm Gear (Worm Wheel)
h1: Husqvarna Worm Wheel for 550XP Mark II
meta: Husqvarna 550XP Mark II oil pump worm gear, listed as the worm wheel. Replace a worn gear when the bar stops oiling and protect your bar and chain.
tagline: The worm gear that drives the oil pump on the 550XP Mark II.
summary: The Husqvarna 550XP Mark II oil pump worm gear, called the worm wheel in Husqvarna parts lists, drives the bar oil pump from the crankshaft. When its teeth wear or strip, the pump stops turning and the bar and chain run dry, which ruins both fast.
highlights: Replacement oil pump drive gear for the 550XP Mark II
Fixes a bar that isn't getting oil
Protects the bar and chain from dry running
Small part, big difference in bar life

p: If the bar is dry, the chain smokes or turns blue, or there is no oil flick when you run the saw at a stump, the oil system needs a look. Start simple: check the oil tank, filter, bar oil hole and the oil port in the bar. If those are clear, the worm gear may be worn or stripped.
Worn worm gears are common on saws that see lots of hours, especially if the chain has been run dry.

Many oiling problems are caused by a clogged oil port in the bar or a blocked oil filter, so check those first. If the oil level never drops, or the chain stays dry even with a clean bar and full tank, the worm gear or pump is likely at fault. The 550XP Mark II is a popular saw for limbing and bucking, so keeping its oil system working is important for bar and chain life.
Remove the bar, chain, clutch and possibly the oil pump to access the gear. Check the pump drive while you are there. Install the new gear, reassemble and check for oil flow.
Running a saw without bar oil wears the bar and chain quickly. See more 550XP Mark II parts in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Why isn't my 550XP Mark II oiling the bar?
faq.a: Check the oil tank, filter and bar oil port first. If those are clear, a worn worm gear or pump may be the cause.

faq.q: Do I need to remove the clutch to replace the worm wheel?
faq.a: Usually yes. The gear sits behind the clutch on the crankshaft.

name: Husqvarna Worm Wheel for 562XP
title: Husqvarna 562XP Oil Pump Worm Gear (Worm Wheel)
h1: Husqvarna Worm Wheel for 562XP
meta: Husqvarna 562XP oil pump worm gear, listed as the worm wheel. Replace a stripped gear when your 60 cc saw stops oiling and save your bar and chain.
tagline: The worm gear that drives the bar oil pump on the 562XP.
summary: The Husqvarna 562XP oil pump worm gear, listed as the worm wheel in Husqvarna parts lists, drives the bar oil pump from the crankshaft. When it wears or strips, the oil pump stops turning, the bar runs dry, and the chain and bar wear out fast.
highlights: Replacement oil pump drive gear for the 562XP
Fixes a bar that isn't oiling
Protects the bar and chain from dry running
Original-fit part

body.h: Signs of a worn worm wheel
p: The 562XP is a common felling and bucking saw on tree crews. If it stops putting oil on the bar, start by checking the oil level, filter and bar oil port. If those are fine, a stripped worm gear is a likely cause.
Dry running quickly blues the chain, wears the bar rails and kills the nose sprocket, so fix oiling problems right away.

A worm gear can wear quickly if the oil tank is run dry, if dirty bar oil is used, or if the clutch is overheated. Use clean bar oil, keep the tank filled whenever you fuel up, and check the bar's oil hole every time you change the chain. Those simple habits help the worm gear and oil pump last much longer. A properly oiled bar and chain cut faster and last longer.
Remove the bar, chain and clutch to access the gear. Inspect the oil pump for wear at the same time. Install the new gear, reassemble and check oil flow at a stump before working.
With the clutch off, also check the clutch drum, needle bearing and sprocket for wear, since they come apart in the same job and are often due at the same time.
Find more 562XP parts, including mufflers and knee joint assemblies, in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Why does my 562XP stop oiling?
faq.a: A clogged oil port, blocked filter, worn worm gear or failing pump are common causes.

faq.q: Is the worm wheel the same as on the 550XP Mark II?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Order the part listed for your exact saw model.

name: Inside Felling Dog for 572XP
title: Husqvarna 572XP Felling Dog, Inside: Bumper Spike
h1: Inside Felling Dog for 572XP
meta: Husqvarna 572XP felling dog for the inside position. Replace worn or bent bumper spikes so the saw pivots cleanly and holds steady in big cuts.
tagline: The inner bumper spike for the 572XP. Grip and pivot point for big cuts.
summary: This Husqvarna 572XP felling dog is the inside spike that sits next to the bar mount, giving the saw a pivot point against the wood. A sharp, solid felling dog makes bucking and felling cuts more controlled and less tiring, and worn or bent dogs slip on the bark.
highlights: Inside felling dog (bumper spike) for the 572XP
Gives a solid pivot point for bucking and felling cuts
Replaces worn, dull or bent dogs
Pairs with the outer felling dog

p: When you are felling or bucking big wood, the felling dogs hold the saw against the log so you can pivot through the cut instead of muscling it. Dull or bent spikes slip, which makes cuts slower and less controlled.
The inside dog sits closest to the bar and takes a lot of wear. If it is rounded, bent or loose, replace it.

Felling dogs also protect the saw body. When you are bucking big logs, the dog takes the pressure instead of the clutch cover or the saw housing. A worn dog can let the saw slide or rock, which can lead to pinching or kickback in some cuts. Replace it when the spikes are rounded or bent, and keep the mounting screws tight. A good dog makes long days of felling and bucking easier.
Remove the bar and chain, take off the old dog, and fit the new one with the correct screws, tightened to spec. Check the outer dog at the same time.
Use the correct Husqvarna screws for the dog, since a screw that is too long can interfere with parts behind it. Check that the bar and chain sit and run freely once everything is back together.
Keep felling dogs tight, since a loose one can shift into the chain path. Find more 572XP parts in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: What is the difference between inside and outside felling dogs?
faq.a: The inside dog sits next to the bar and the outside dog bolts on outside it. Many saws use both.

faq.q: Do I need to remove the bar to replace it?
faq.a: Usually yes. Remove the bar and chain to reach the mounting screws.

name: Muffler for Husqvarna 562XP Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 562XP Muffler: Replacement Exhaust
h1: Muffler for Husqvarna 562XP Chainsaw
meta: Replacement Husqvarna 562XP muffler for the 60 cc saw. Swap a cracked, rattling or damaged muffler and keep exhaust heat directed away from you.
tagline: A replacement muffler for the 562XP when the old one cracks or rattles.
summary: This Husqvarna 562XP muffler replaces a cracked, damaged or worn muffler on the 562XP. A muffler that is loose or broken can let hot exhaust and sparks go where they shouldn't, increase noise, and damage nearby parts, so replace it when it starts to fail.
highlights: Replacement muffler for the 562XP
Fixes cracked, broken or rattling mufflers
Directs exhaust heat away from the operator
Fit with a new gasket

p: Mufflers take heat and vibration all day, and on a busy felling and bucking saw like the 562XP they can crack around the mounts or the outlet. Signs include a new rattle, soot around seams, exhaust coming from the wrong place, or a louder saw.
Check the spark arrestor screen during routine service, too. A clogged screen costs power.

The 562XP is a 60 cc class saw that sees a lot of hard work on tree crews, and its muffler takes plenty of heat. A damaged muffler can also cause the saw to run poorly. A clogged spark arrestor screen or a cracked baffle can restrict exhaust flow and reduce power. If the saw feels down on power and the muffler is damaged, replacing it may restore performance. Keep the screen clean.

Let the saw cool fully. Remove the top cover and old muffler, clean the cylinder face and fit a new gasket. Mount the new muffler and tighten the screws to the torque in the service manual. Recheck the screws after the first hours of running.
Never run a saw with a damaged muffler, as hot exhaust and sparks can be a fire hazard. More 562XP parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Should I replace the muffler gasket too?
faq.a: Yes. Fit a new gasket whenever the muffler comes off.

faq.q: Can a damaged muffler affect saw performance?
faq.a: Yes. Leaks, a clogged screen or damage can affect running, noise and heat.

name: Muffler Gasket for Husqvarna 372XP X-Torque Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 372XP Muffler Gasket for X-Torque Saws
h1: Muffler Gasket for Husqvarna 372XP X-Torque Chainsaw
meta: Husqvarna 372XP muffler gasket for the X-Torque. Replace a burnt or torn gasket to stop exhaust leaks and keep the muffler sealing on your 70 cc saw.
tagline: The muffler gasket for the 372XP X-Torque. Fit a new one every time the muffler comes off.
summary: This Husqvarna 372XP muffler gasket seals the muffler to the cylinder on the 372XP X-Torque. A burnt or torn gasket leaks hot exhaust, leaves soot around the cylinder and can let the muffler work loose, so it is a part to replace whenever the muffler is removed.
highlights: Muffler gasket for the 372XP X-Torque
Stops exhaust leaks at the cylinder
Replace whenever the muffler is removed
Inexpensive, worth keeping a spare

p: Heat cycles and vibration break down muffler gaskets over time. A loose muffler speeds this up. Signs include soot around the muffler joint, a louder saw, or exhaust leaking near the cylinder.
Gaskets compress when tightened, so an old one rarely seals properly again. Replace it every time the muffler comes off.

The 372XP X-Torque is a 70 cc class saw that runs hot, especially when bucking big wood. That heat breaks down gaskets faster than on smaller saws. Keeping a spare gasket on hand saves you from running a muffler without one, which can lead to leaks and damage. If you are replacing the muffler or checking the piston, always fit a new gasket during reassembly.

Let the saw cool fully. Remove the muffler, clean the cylinder face and muffler flange, and fit the new gasket in the correct orientation. Tighten the muffler screws to spec and recheck after the first few hours of running.
Tighten the muffler screws evenly so the gasket compresses flat all the way around. Uneven torque is a common reason a new gasket leaks. After the saw has run and cooled, check the screws once more.
While the muffler is off, inspect the piston through the exhaust port for scoring. More 372XP parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Can I reuse the old muffler gasket?
faq.a: It is not recommended. Gaskets compress and usually don't seal properly again.

faq.q: Is this gasket the same as for the older 372XP?
faq.a: Not always. Order the part listed for the X-Torque model.

name: Needle Bearing for 3/8 Pitch Chainsaw Clutch Drum
title: Chainsaw Clutch Needle Bearing for 3/8 Pitch Drums
h1: Needle Bearing for 3/8 Pitch Chainsaw Clutch Drum
meta: Chainsaw clutch needle bearing for 3/8 pitch clutch drums. Replace a worn bearing to stop wobble, heat and early clutch drum wear on your saw.
tagline: A needle bearing for 3/8 pitch clutch drums. Replace it when you replace the drum.
summary: This chainsaw clutch needle bearing fits inside the clutch drum on saws running 3/8 inch pitch chain, letting the drum spin freely on the crankshaft when the clutch is disengaged. A worn bearing causes drum wobble, heat and early wear, and it can damage the crankshaft.
highlights: Needle bearing for 3/8 pitch clutch drums
Fixes drum wobble, noise and heat
Replace with every new clutch drum or rim sprocket
Check fit for your saw model

p: The clutch drum spins on this bearing whenever the engine is idling and the chain is stopped. Once it wears, the drum can wobble, run hot, or chatter, and the chain may creep at idle. Over time a bad bearing wears the crankshaft as well.
Grease it lightly at regular service intervals, especially on saws that idle a lot.

Old listings sometimes say 3/8 gauge, but 3/8 inch is a chain pitch, not a gauge. This bearing is used with clutch drums for 3/8 pitch chain on many saws. Bearing size depends on the saw's crankshaft and the drum, not just the chain pitch, so check your saw model before ordering. A new bearing is cheap insurance whenever you replace the clutch drum or rim sprocket.

Remove the bar, chain and clutch to reach the drum. Slide the old bearing off the crank, clean the area, and fit the new one with a little grease. Check the drum and sprocket for wear, and replace them if needed.
Wipe the crank clean before fitting, use a light coat of grease rather than heavy packing, and make sure the drum spins freely once the clutch is back on.
Confirm the bearing fits your saw model, since crankshaft and drum sizes vary. More parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: How do I know if the needle bearing is worn?
faq.a: Drum wobble, heat, noise or a chain that creeps at idle are common signs.

faq.q: Should I replace the bearing with a new clutch drum?
faq.a: Yes. Fitting a new bearing with a new drum is good practice.
